summary.fr: Au Pays basque nord, Zan Pantzar, figure du carnaval jouée par un acteur ou un mannequin, est promené, jugé puis condamné un samedi de la période grasse ou le soir du Mardi gras, comme à Ustaritz ; la farce marque le passage de l'hiver au Carême.

summary.en: Linked to the former Dauphiné, the rigodon is a lively tune and dance in duple time, historically played on the fiddle and danced in twos, fours, sixes or more with foot stamps; folk groups and trad ball musicians keep it alive today.

summary.en: In the Grands-Fonds of Grande-Terre (Guadeloupe), the wake held after a death gathers neighbours and friends for unaccompanied songs, riddles in Creole and French and agility games led by a soloist, to support the bereaved family.

summary.en: Born with home computing in the 1980s, the French demoscene brings together coders, artists and musicians who make demos, non-commercial programs rendered in real time, and show them in competitions at gatherings called demoparties.

summary.fr: L'affouage permet aux habitants d'une commune ou d'une section de commune de couper chaque année, dans la forêt collective, du bois de chauffage ou de construction pour leur seul usage, sans pouvoir le revendre ; il reste vivant notamment en Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes, en Lorraine et en Bourgogne-Franche-Comté.
summary.en: Affouage lets the residents of a commune or commune section cut firewood or building timber each year in their collective forest, for their own use only and never for sale; it remains common in Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes, Lorraine and Burgundy-Franche-Comté.

summary.en: In the Doubs, each canton holds a yearly agricultural show, a contest for the finest livestock combined with a village festival; it moves from village to village, so each one hosts it roughly every twenty years.

summary.fr: En Périgord, le conte occitan mêle contes traditionnels, dont les histoires facétieuses appelées viòrlas ou nhòrlas, et créations de conteurs ; longtemps transmis en famille et au village, il vit aujourd'hui surtout sur scène et se fait plus rare.
summary.en: In Périgord, Occitan storytelling combines traditional tales, notably the comic stories called viòrlas or nhòrlas, with tellers' own creations; long passed on in families and villages, it now lives mainly on stage and is becoming rarer.

summary.en: In Lot-et-Garonne, a handful of amateur and professional storytellers keep tales alive in Occitan or bilingually; the comic figure of the mock-simple country fellow dominates, and some mix their stories with traditional or home-made instruments.

summary.en: In Daglan (Dordogne), an amateur company performs a new play in Occitan each year, written and staged locally, in the village and nearby; heir to the Félibrige revival, the practice is gradually being taken up by younger people.

summary.en: In Brittany, "café evenings" regularly gather traditional singers and storytellers, often once a month, around the tables of a café, with no stage, microphone or line-up: anyone may sing or tell a tale when they wish.

summary.en: In the Trégor and Goëlo areas of the Côtes-d'Armor, a dozen local associations hold free evening gatherings each season in village halls, where volunteer singers, storytellers and musicians perform in turn, often in Breton; the format was revived in the early 1990s.

summary.fr: À La Réunion, le rakontaz zistoir réunit un conteur et son public autour de contes, légendes, proverbes, chants et devinettes (sirandane) en créole, avec formules rituelles d'ouverture et de clôture ; après un déclin dans les années 1960-1970, la pratique a repris vigueur.
summary.en: On Réunion, rakontaz zistoir brings a storyteller and audience together around Creole tales, legends, proverbs, songs and riddles (sirandane), framed by ritual opening and closing lines; after a decline in the 1960s and 70s it has revived.

summary.fr: À Ouvéa, dans les îles Loyauté (Nouvelle-Calédonie), le seloo est un chant polyphonique a cappella, le plus souvent à quatre voix d'hommes, aux harmonies réputées « dissonantes » ; chanté en toutes circonstances, il porte les langues iaai et fagauvea.
summary.en: On Ouvéa, in the Loyalty Islands (New Caledonia), the seloo is an a cappella polyphonic song, usually for four male voices, known for its "dissonant" harmonies; sung on any occasion, it carries the Iaai and Fagauvea languages.

summary.fr: À Lifou, dans les îles Loyauté (Nouvelle-Calédonie), l'anethem est un chant religieux mixte à quatre voix, introduit par les missionnaires protestants vers 1840 et noté en tonic sol-fa ; chanté entre les lectures du culte, il accompagne aussi des événements coutumiers.
summary.en: On Lifou, in the Loyalty Islands (New Caledonia), the anethem is a four-part mixed-voice hymn brought by Protestant missionaries around 1840 and written in tonic sol-fa; sung between Bible readings, it also accompanies customary events.

summary.en: In the Basque Country, bertsolaritza is an improvised verbal contest, rhymed and sung unaccompanied in Basque: bertsolaris respond to a theme set by a host at village fêtes, carnivals and championships.

summary.en: French falconry is the art of hunting wild game with trained birds of prey; practised in France since at least the 5th century, it declined with firearms before enthusiasts revived it from the 19th century onwards.

summary.en: French-tradition horsemanship, kept alive by the Cadre Noir of the national riding school in Saumur (Maine-et-Loire), seeks lightness and the horse's cooperation through discreet aids; it is passed on mainly in person from riding master to pupils, both riders and horses.

summary.en: In the Camargue and nearby villages, the course camarguaise puts the bull, the biòu, in the spotlight: in the arena, white-clad raseteurs try to snatch the rosette and strings from its horns, framed by the morning sorting, the abrivado and the bandido.

summary.en: In the Basque Country, bare-hand pelota is played in a trinquet, an enclosed court where players, singly or in pairs, strike the ball against the front wall; a bevelled corner and a square hole, the xilo, deflect it unpredictably.

summary.en: Practised across France, savate or French boxing is a combat sport using only the fists and the feet, which wear special shoes; bouts are fought either as "assaut", where full-power blows are banned, or as "combat".

summary.en: Played since the 1870s around Paris, notably in the Bois de Vincennes, the jeu de boules parisien, once called "jeu de berges", is played on covered or open-air grounds in about ten suburban towns, with the bowls always rolled.

summary.en: In Picardy, Île-de-France and Champagne, the bouquet provincial brings archery companies to a town decorated for their parade, usually on a Sunday in May, and opens a months-long season of Beursault shooting contests.

summary.fr: Surtout présent en Picardie et en Île-de-France, le tir Beursault est une forme traditionnelle de tir à l'arc pratiquée dans un « jeu d'arc », où l'archer tire alternativement vers deux cibles opposées, selon un cérémonial et des règles de courtoisie propres aux compagnies d'arc.
summary.en: Found mainly in Picardy and Île-de-France, Beursault is a traditional form of archery practised on a "jeu d'arc", where archers shoot in turn at two facing targets, following a ceremonial and code of courtesy kept by archery companies.

summary.en: Born in the Mont Blanc massif in the 18th century with peasant guides, mountaineering is the art of climbing rock, snow and ice faces with modest means, self-reliance and shared values; Chamonix-Mont-Blanc led its listing.

summary.en: In Fontainebleau and Paris, real tennis (courte paume) is played in an enclosed court: players hit the ball with a racket over a net, and the walls and sloping roofs of the court are part of play; professional masters pass on its intricate rules.

summary.en: In the Nord, where most fanciers come from mining families, pigeon racing means breeding and selecting ringed homing pigeons that are released far away in weekly contests; the winner is the owner whose bird reaches its loft first.

summary.en: Common in French Flanders and northern Pas-de-Calais, vertical popinjay shooting has archers shoot down feathered wooden "birds" perched atop a 25 to 30 metre pole; the higher the bird, the more points it scores.

summary.en: Practised in Gruissan (Aude) and many other harbours, from Marseille to Collioure and as far as Strasbourg, traditional rowing consists of 300-metre races in which two heavy wooden boats, each with six rowers and a cox, turn round a buoy.

summary.en: In Arras (Pas-de-Calais), water jousting takes place on the Scarpe basin using a local method: although the boats have engines, the crews pull them towards each other along ropes stretched beside the canal before the jousters clash.

summary.en: In Accolay (Yonne) and Clamecy (Nièvre), water jousting follows local methods with identical rules, alongside the Paris method used in championships: standing on the rear platform of a red or blue boat, each jouster must push the other into the water.

summary.en: Along the coasts of Roussillon, Languedoc, Provence and Corsica, fishermen, boatbuilders and associations still sail under the lateen sail, a triangular sail hung from a long yard. The skills pass from hand to hand, notably at boat gatherings.

summary.en: In the Landes, the Gers and neighbouring Gascony, the course landaise pits dodgers and leapers against wild cows in village arenas, evading each charge with a pivot or a jump, to the sound of brass bandas at local festivals.

summary.en: In Brittany, the fiddle is played in two ways in music from the oral tradition: solo, in the manner of the old "sonneurs" or village fiddlers, or within bands born of the folk revival; players number in the low thousands.

summary.en: In Brittany, the accordion, mostly chromatic in Lower Brittany and diatonic in Upper Brittany, took root between 1880 and 1930; thousands of musicians play it today, solo in the "sonneur" style or in bands, chiefly at fest-noz dances.

summary.en: In Redon (Ille-et-Vilaine), on the fourth Sunday of October during the old "teillouse" fair, the Bogue d'or contest has gathered some forty traditional singers since 1975, chosen at singing gatherings held across Upper Brittany.

summary.en: Across much of central and southern Brittany, in call-and-response singing a leader sings each phrase and the whole group repeats it in unison; it is used for walking, dancing and table songs, and lives on today at fest-noz dances and singing evenings.

summary.en: In Carbuccia (Corse-du-Sud), the confraternity's cantors sing the services for the living and the dead and those of Holy Week in paghjella, three-voice unaccompanied male polyphony; their "composite" versu borrows from other versi on top of its own pattern.

summary.en: A symbol of Guadeloupean identity, gwoka combines call-and-response singing in Creole, rhythms played on ka drums and a solo dancer in dialogue with the lead makè drum; it is shared especially at léwòz, night gatherings open to all.

elements.title_fr: Le balèt de Tende (Alpes-Maritimes)

summary.fr: À Tende (Alpes-Maritimes), le balèt est une danse de couple sautée, jouée par un duo accordéon et clarinette : sans phase de progression, le couple reste sur place et alterne face-à-face et rotation ; plus fatigant, il est bien moins dansé que la courenta.
summary.en: In Tende (Alpes-Maritimes), the balèt is a hopping couple dance played by an accordion and clarinet duo: with no forward phase, the couple stays in place, alternating face-to-face steps and spins; more tiring, it is danced far less than the courenta.

summary.en: In Tende (Alpes-Maritimes), the courenta is a hopping couple dance at village balls, played by a chromatic accordion and clarinet duo; it links three figures, circling forward, face to face and spinning, and alternates with the balèt.

summary.en: A carillon is an instrument of at least 23 tuned bells, played from a keyboard struck with the fists and a pedalboard; France has several dozen, from the North to Savoy, where carillonneurs perform concerts and tunes from belfries and church towers.

summary.en: A coiled natural horn that appeared at the French court in the late 17th century for royal hunts, the trompe is now sounded across France by thousands of players in groups and schools, with a repertoire of fanfares that has grown since the 18th century.

summary.en: In Lower Brittany, kan ha diskan is a Breton-language dance song in which two singers alternate, each picking up the end of the other's line; once passed on within families, it was taken up by younger singers through fest-noz dances and field recordings.

summary.en: In Upper Brittany, at Easter and on the night before 1 May, small groups go from house to house singing a song tied to the feast, the Passion or the May song, and are given eggs or money in return once they have sung it through.

summary.en: The cabrette, or musette, is an Auvergne bagpipe without a drone, played solo while the piper beats time with the feet; it is heard in Auvergne and nearby regions and in Paris, where it plays for dancing at community banquets.

summary.en: In Île-de-France, notably in Paris and Villeneuve-Saint-Georges, the Georgian community passes on Georgia's folk dances. Each region has its own, such as the Kartuli or the Khorumi, with their own costumes, music and songs.

summary.en: In Île-de-France, the Portuguese diaspora keeps fado alive, an urban song born in 19th-century Lisbon that blends music, singing and poetry. It is traditionally performed by a solo voice with two guitars, one of them the Portuguese guitar.

image.alt: La lutte bretonne / Gouren

summary.fr: Le gouren, lutte traditionnelle de Bretagne, se pratique debout : agrippés à la chemise de l'adversaire, les lutteurs cherchent à le projeter sur le dos ; arbitrage et serment se font en breton, et les tournois d'été à l'ancienne peuvent avoir un bélier pour enjeu.
summary.en: Gouren, the traditional wrestling of Brittany, is fought standing: gripping each other's shirt, wrestlers try to throw their opponent flat on his back; refereeing and the oath are in Breton, and old-style summer tournaments may have a ram as the prize.

summary.en: Recovered in Quistinic (Morbihan), this game of skill has five pins hung from a horizontal bar: when struck by the ball, each one swings round and locks onto a second bar. It is now played at fêtes of the bilingual schools in Lanester.

summary.en: In the countryside of the Pays Pagan (northern Finistère), the "ar mestr" ball served as the jack: players threw metal balls of any weight towards this wooden ball, on ground with no boundaries. Still common before 1939, the game gave way to pétanque.

summary.en: In Maine-et-Loire, sand bowls is played with wooden balls thrown from one sand-filled box into another, where the jack lies; the side boards are part of the game, which is learnt by watching and playing within small clubs.

summary.en: In Saint-Sébastien-sur-Loire, Nantes sand bowls is played on a covered lane filled with 80 cm of Loire sand, raked before each game; the black wooden balls, striped or plain depending on the team, are often thrown to hit the opponent's balls directly.

summary.en: Typical of the Nantes area, boule nantaise is played on an asphalt lane with curved edges and a board, the "talon", at each end: the ball, always rolled, may bounce off it back towards the jack; play takes place in a bowling hall or in café back rooms.

summary.en: In the Morbihan, Breton bowls is played on a board-edged ground of grass or hard sand: to knock away an opponent's ball, players roll it or throw it "à pok" or "à demi-pok", always open-handed; a county committee has federated the clubs since 1936.

summary.en: In the Morlaix area of north Finistère and in Guérande, lead-weighted bowls are rolled along sanded alleys edged with wooden boards; each ball holds five lead plugs, four to keep it straight and a fifth, the "fort", that bends its path.

summary.en: Originating in the Quimper area, boultenn is a shooting game: from about 8.5 m, a player throws six balls to knock three balls off a wooden block where they sit in hollows, the centre one scoring double; landing exactly in place of the ejected ball doubles the score.

elements.title_fr: La galoche bigoudène

location_sources.publisher: PCI Lab (ministère de la Culture, CIRDOC)

image.alt: La galoche bigoudène

summary.fr: Mentionnée à Quimper dès 1388, la galoche bigoudène consiste à lancer de lourds palets d'acier pour abattre un cylindre de bois, la galoche, surmonté d'une rondelle, le lipar ; le point va au palet le plus proche du lipar une fois tombé, et les concours ont lieu en galochodromes.
summary.en: Mentioned in Quimper as early as 1388, galoche bigoudène involves throwing heavy steel discs to knock over a wooden cylinder, the galoche, topped with a small washer, the lipar; the point goes to the disc nearest the fallen lipar, and contests take place on purpose-built grounds.

summary.en: An Anjou game that became a sport in the late 19th century, played for instance in Mazé (Maine-et-Loire), boule de fort uses a 25-metre trough-shaped track: the slow, wobbling bowl follows curved paths to get close to the jack.

summary.en: On the north coast of Finistère, around Saint-Pol-de-Léon, each player throws a cast-iron palet to topple the galoche, a wooden peg standing on the ground about fifteen paces away, then a second one to land as close as possible to the coin that leant against it.

summary.en: In the Brière and on the Guérande peninsula, players staked coins on the galoche, or bique, then tried to knock it down with steel palets often cut from shipyard bars; dropped around the 1980s, the game is now revived at association-run events.

summary.fr: D'origine hollandaise mais très pratiqué dans toute la Bretagne, le billard hollandais consiste à faire glisser trente palets de bois sur un long plateau jusque dans quatre cases à trous valant de 1 à 4 points ; une série complète d'un palet par case rapporte un bonus.
summary.en: Dutch in origin but widely played across Brittany, Dutch billiards involves sliding thirty wooden discs along a long board into four slotted compartments worth 1 to 4 points; a full set of one disc in each compartment earns a bonus.

elements.title_fr: Le birinig

location_sources.publisher: PCI Lab (ministère de la Culture, CIRDOC)

image.credit: Ludibreizh29
image.alt: Le birinig

summary.fr: Attesté de longue date dans l'ouest de la Bretagne, le birinig est un jeu de quilles de table : une boule suspendue par une ficelle à un mât doit contourner celui-ci avant d'abattre neuf quilles ; on joue en 101 points, un peu comme aux fléchettes anglaises.
summary.en: Long attested in western Brittany, birinig is a table skittles game: a ball hanging by a string from a post must swing round it before knocking down nine pins; games are played to 101 points, somewhat like English darts.

location_sources.publisher: PCI Lab (ministère de la Culture, CIRDOC)

summary.fr: Populaire en Ille-et-Vilaine, la boîte à cases est un jeu dérivé du palet : on lance des palets en fonte dans une boîte en bois en trapèze divisée en cinq cases, la plus petite valant 5 points ; on y joue aux kermesses, aux fêtes de village et en marge des concours de palet.
summary.en: Popular in Ille-et-Vilaine, the box game is an offshoot of palet: players toss cast-iron discs into a trapezoid wooden box split into five compartments, the smallest worth 5 points; it is played at fêtes, village fairs and alongside palet contests.

location_sources.publisher: PCI Lab (ministère de la Culture, CIRDOC)

summary.fr: Jeu de boules breton dont Plouégat-Guerrand serait le dernier foyer, la boule montante consiste à faire rouler une boule le plus haut possible sur un plan incliné sans la faire tomber au sommet ; une version connue à Argol demande plutôt de la faire passer dans un trou.
summary.en: A Breton bowls game whose last stronghold is said to be Plouégat-Guerrand, the climbing ball involves rolling a ball as high as possible up a slope without letting it drop off the top; a version known in Argol instead requires sending it through a hole.

elements.title_fr: Le jeu de la boule pendante

location_sources.publisher: PCI Lab (ministère de la Culture, CIRDOC)

image.alt: Le jeu de la boule pendante

summary.fr: Jeu attribué à la Bretagne sans lieu d'origine précis, la boule pendante consiste à toucher une boule de bois suspendue à une potence en lançant trois boules ; à chaque réussite, le joueur recule d'un mètre, et toucher le fil annule le lancer.
summary.en: Attributed to Brittany with no precise place of origin, the hanging ball game consists in hitting a wooden ball hung from a gallows-like frame with three thrown balls; after each hit the player steps back a metre, and touching the string voids the throw.

location_sources.publisher: PCI Lab (ministère de la Culture, CIRDOC)

summary.fr: Connu dans toute l'Europe mais très pratiqué en Bretagne, le jeu de la grenouille consiste à lancer des palets de fonte dans la gueule ouverte d'une grenouille en métal fixée sur un meuble en bois percé de trous ; les palets tombent dans des casiers qui indiquent les points.
summary.en: Known across Europe but much played in Brittany, the frog game involves tossing cast-iron discs into the open mouth of a metal frog set on a wooden cabinet pierced with holes; the discs drop into slots showing the points scored.

summary.fr: Populaire en Ille-et-Vilaine, le jeu du sabot, dérivé du palet, consiste à lancer des palets en fonte dans un sabot posé au sol, suspendu ou fixé à une planche ; dans certaines versions, le poids des palets fait basculer un levier qui révèle une bouteille à gagner.
summary.en: Popular in Ille-et-Vilaine, the clog game, derived from palet, involves tossing cast-iron discs into a wooden clog set on the ground, hung up or fixed to a board; in some versions the weight of the discs tips a lever that reveals a bottle as the prize.

summary.en: In Ille-et-Vilaine, target palet is a precision game offered at local fêtes: from about 6 m, players toss discs onto a square board painted with coloured concentric rings, the centre worth 4 points, and a disc counts only if it stays on the board.

summary.en: Played in the Gallo country of eastern Brittany, palet on a holed board involves tossing five discs that must land flat on a board pierced with holes, each worth a different number of points; it is played singly or in teams.

summary.fr: Jeu de précision d'origine bretonne, le trou du chat ou patigo consiste à faire rouler une boule à travers un trou à peine plus grand qu'elle, percé dans une planche verticale ; à chaque réussite, le joueur recule d'un mètre, et le plus éloigné après dix lancers l'emporte.
summary.en: A precision game of Breton origin, the cat's hole or patigo consists in rolling a ball through a hole barely larger than itself cut in an upright board; after each success the player steps back a metre, and whoever ends farthest away after ten throws wins.

summary.en: In Cornouaille, kilhou koz consists in knocking down the "old woman", the central pin worth nine points, as often as possible among nine pins set out in a rectangle; to count, the ball must roll under a string stretched in front of the pins.

summary.fr: En Bresse, notamment à Saint-Étienne-du-Bois (Ain), le jeu de sept quilles se joue surtout pour de petites mises : un lancer ne compte que si la boule abat d'abord la « première », la quille placée dans l'axe de la piste.
summary.en: In the Bresse, for instance in Saint-Étienne-du-Bois (Ain), the seven-pin skittles game is mostly played for small stakes: a throw only counts if the ball first knocks down the "first" pin, the one in line with the alley.

elements.title_fr: Les jeux et sports athlétiques bretons

location_sources.publisher: PCI Lab (ministère de la Culture, CIRDOC)

summary.fr: Dans les cinq départements de la Bretagne historique, les jeux athlétiques bretons, issus des durs travaux ruraux, réunissent sept épreuves de championnat, dont le lancer d'un poids de 20 kg, le lever d'un essieu de charrette et le lancer d'une gerbe de paille à la fourche.
summary.en: Across the five departments of historic Brittany, Breton athletic games, rooted in hard farm labour, comprise seven championship events, including throwing a 20 kg weight, lifting a cart axle and pitching a sheaf of straw over a bar with a fork.

summary_source.publisher: PCI Lab (ministère de la Culture, CIRDOC)

elements.title_fr: Les jeux de force du Trégor

location_sources.publisher: PCI Lab (ministère de la Culture, CIRDOC)

image.credit: Fiche d'inventaire du PCI (ministère de la Culture), via PCI Lab
image.alt: Les jeux de force du Trégor

summary.fr: Dans le Trégor (Côtes-d'Armor), des jeux de force traditionnels aux noms bretons perpétuent des gestes du travail paysan : charger un sac de sable sur l'épaule, dresser une perche en l'appuyant sur la cuisse, soulever d'une main un essieu de charrette.
summary.en: In the Trégor area of the Côtes-d'Armor, traditional strength games with Breton names carry on gestures of farm work: hoisting a sandbag onto the shoulder, raising a pole upright by bracing it against the thigh, lifting a cart axle with one hand.

elements.title_fr: La lutte traditionnelle basque

location_sources.publisher: PCI Lab (ministère de la Culture, CIRDOC)

image.alt: La lutte traditionnelle basque

summary.fr: Au Pays basque, la borroka est une lutte inspirée d'anciennes formes locales et pratiquée depuis 2009 : les adversaires se tiennent par la ceinture et chacun tente de repousser l'autre jusqu'au béret posé au fond de son camp, au son de la txalaparta.
summary.en: In the Basque Country, borroka is a wrestling style inspired by older local forms and practised since 2009: opponents grip each other's belt and each tries to push the other back to the beret set at the end of their lane, to the sound of the txalaparta.

summary_source.publisher: PCI Lab (ministère de la Culture, CIRDOC)

elements.title_fr: Les régates de traînières

location_sources.publisher: PCI Lab (ministère de la Culture, CIRDOC)

image.credit: Etxeko
image.alt: Les régates de traînières

summary.fr: Sur la côte basque, d'Hendaye à Anglet, des équipages de treize rameurs et un barreur s'affrontent en traînière, ancien bateau de pêche de douze mètres devenu bateau de course, sur un parcours en mer avec virage autour d'une bouée.
summary.en: On the Basque coast, from Hendaye to Anglet, crews of thirteen rowers and a cox race traineras, twelve-metre former fishing boats turned racing craft, on a sea course with a turn around a buoy.

elements.title_fr: La force basque

summary.fr: Au Pays basque, la « force basque » (herri kirolak) regroupe des épreuves de force et d'adresse issues des anciens travaux des champs, comme le lever de pierre ou de charrette ; concours et démonstrations ont lieu chaque semaine en été.
summary.en: In the Basque Country, "Basque strength" (herri kirolak) covers trials of strength and skill drawn from old farm work, such as lifting stones or a cart; contests and displays are held every week in summer.

elements.title_fr: Le jeu de pelote basque

location_sources.publisher: PCI Lab (ministère de la Culture, CIRDOC)

summary.fr: Le laxoa, plus ancien jeu de pelote basque encore joué, oppose sur la place du village deux équipes gantées de cuir qui se renvoient la balle de part et d'autre d'une ligne ; côté français, il ne se joue plus qu'une ou deux fois par an.
summary.en: Laxoa, the oldest form of Basque pelota still played, pits two teams wearing leather gloves against each other across a line on the village square; in the French Basque Country it is now played only once or twice a year.

summary_source.publisher: PCI Lab (ministère de la Culture, CIRDOC)

location_sources.publisher: Ministère de la Culture, fiche d'inventaire

summary.fr: Le rebot est une spécialité de pelote basque jouée en plein air sur une grande place, au Pays basque et en Béarn : deux équipes de cinq se renvoient la pelote de part et d'autre d'une ligne mobile, le plus souvent le dimanche matin de mars à octobre.
summary.en: Rebot is an open-air form of Basque pelota played on a large square in the French Basque Country and Béarn: two teams of five return the ball across a shifting dividing line, usually on Sunday mornings from March to October.

summary_source.publisher: Fiche d'inventaire (ministère de la Culture)

summary.en: In the Landes, the wooden stilts once used by shepherds have become a pastime: folk-group members and racers compete in sprints, long-distance treks and an obstacle course held during the Dax festivities.

image.alt: Les quilles de trois en Aquitaine

summary.fr: Dans le bas Adour, les quilles de trois se jouent en plein air sur un quillier de gravillons : avec une lourde boule de bois cerclée de fer, on vise trois quilles alignées à cinq mètres l'une de l'autre, dont la plus grosse est appelée « la vieille ».
summary.en: In the lower Adour valley, three-pin skittles is played outdoors on a gravel alley: with a heavy iron-bound wooden ball, players aim at three pins set five metres apart, the largest of them known as "the old one".

summary.en: In Aquitaine, chiefly in the Landes and Béarn, six-pin skittles requires knocking down exactly five of the six pins with up to three throws of a wooden ball; it is played both for fun and in federation championships.

summary.en: In the Landes, Pyrénées-Atlantiques and Hautes-Pyrénées, players of nine-pin skittles strike the "hand pin" with a heavy handled ball so that it knocks down the others in twelve set figures; the old game is now an organised sport.

summary.fr: Au Pays basque, le pasaka est une spécialité de pelote jouée en trinquet par deux équipes de deux, qui se renvoient la balle par-dessus un filet avec un gant de cuir ; le geste de renvoi, le xirrist, en fait l'attrait.
summary.en: In the Basque Country, pasaka is a form of pelota played in a trinquet by two pairs who return the ball over a net with a leather glove; much of its appeal lies in the sweeping return stroke called the xirrist.

elements.title_fr: La bague en boghei de Gémenos

location_sources.publisher: PCI Lab (ministère de la Culture, CIRDOC)

image.credit: Chloé Rosati-Marzetti
image.alt: La bague en boghei de Gémenos

summary.fr: À Gémenos, le lundi suivant la Saint-Éloi, des joueurs juchés sur un boghei tiré par un cheval tentent de passer une perche dans le trou d'une planche sans renverser le seau d'eau suspendu au-dessus ; le jeu, presque impossible à gagner, sert surtout à se rafraîchir.
summary.en: In Gémenos, on the Monday after the Saint Eligius feast, players riding a horse-drawn cart try to push a pole through a hole in a board without tipping the bucket of water hung above; almost unwinnable, the game is mainly a way to cool off.

summary.fr: Né à Veynes (Hautes-Alpes) dans les années 1930 et joué aussi à Gap, ce jeu suit les règles de la pétanque mais avec des cubes de bois : leur trajectoire imprévisible sur des terrains en pente favorise le jeu et la bonne humeur plus que la compétition.
summary.en: Born in Veynes (Hautes-Alpes) in the 1930s and also played in Gap, this game follows pétanque rules but uses wooden cubes; their unpredictable rolls on sloping ground favour fun and banter over competition.

summary.fr: Sur le littoral méditerranéen, de Marseille à Nice, la joute provençale oppose deux jouteurs armés d'une lance, debout sur des barques qui se croisent ; très codifiée, elle mêle honneur de tradition médiévale, fête de village et chutes spectaculaires dans l'eau.
summary.en: Along the Mediterranean coast from Marseille to Nice, Provençal water jousting pits two lance-bearing jousters against each other on passing boats; highly codified, it blends a medieval sense of honour, village festivity and splashing falls.

summary.fr: Dans le pays niçois, la mourra est un jeu de doigts où deux adversaires lèvent des doigts en criant un nombre de zéro à dix, pour deviner le total ; un arbitre compte les points sur ses mains, dans un rythme rapide et bruyant.
summary.en: Around Nice, mourra is a finger game in which two opponents raise fingers while shouting a number from zero to ten, trying to call the total; a referee keeps score on his hands, and play is fast and loud.

elements.title_fr: La pétanque

location_sources.publisher: Ministère de la Culture, fiche d'inventaire

summary.fr: Née en Provence au début du XXe siècle comme variante du jeu provençal, la pétanque oppose deux équipes qui lancent des boules métalliques vers un petit but en buis, le « cochonnet » ou « bouchon » ; perdre 13 à 0 vaut le rituel du « baiser de Fanny ».
summary.en: Born in Provence in the early 20th century as a variant of the jeu provençal, pétanque pits two teams throwing metal balls towards a small boxwood jack; losing 13–0 calls for the ritual known as "kissing Fanny".

location_sources.publisher: PCI Lab (ministère de la Culture, CIRDOC)

summary.fr: À Artignosc-sur-Verdon, dernier village provençal où elle se joue, la paume oppose des équipes qui frappent à main nue une balle contre la façade de l'église, en pleine place, sur la chaussée même de la route départementale.
summary.en: In Artignosc-sur-Verdon, the last Provençal village where it survives, the hand-ball game of paume sees teams strike a ball bare-handed against the church front, on the village square and the roadway itself.

elements.title_fr: La pelote basque

location_sources.publisher: PCI Lab (ministère de la Culture, CIRDOC)

summary.fr: Au Plan de Grasse, la pelote basque a pris la suite de la pelote provençale, abandonnée en 1982 ; on y joue à deux contre deux, avec une raquette de bois et une balle en gomme pleine, en trinquet couvert ou sur un fronton en plein air.
summary.en: At Plan de Grasse, Basque pelota took over from Provençal pelota, given up in 1982; it is played two against two with a wooden bat and a solid rubber ball, in a covered trinquet or against an outdoor fronton wall.

elements.title_fr: La rame traditionnelle provençale

location_sources.publisher: PCI Lab (ministère de la Culture, CIRDOC)

summary.fr: Héritée des pêcheurs marseillais, la rame traditionnelle provençale se pratique en compétition sur des barques de 7,20 m à trois bancs fixes et six rames en bois ; distincte de l'aviron, elle exige souffle, force et esprit d'équipe.
summary.en: Inherited from Marseille's fishermen, traditional Provençal rowing is raced in 7.2-metre boats with three fixed benches and six wooden oars; unlike sculling, it calls for stamina, strength and strong team spirit.

elements.title_fr: Le jeu de mus au Pays basque / Mus jokoa

location_sources.publisher: PCI Lab (ministère de la Culture, CIRDOC)

image.credit: Fiche d'inventaire du PCI (ministère de la Culture), via PCI Lab
image.alt: Le jeu de mus au Pays basque / Mus jokoa

summary.fr: Au Pays basque, le mus est un jeu de cartes qui se joue à quatre, en deux équipes, et mêle calcul et bluff ; chaque main se déroule en quatre phases de paris, avec un vocabulaire basque (« paso », « embido », « tira ») et des points souvent comptés avec des haricots.
summary.en: In the Basque Country, mus is a card game for four players in two teams that combines counting and bluffing; each hand has four betting rounds, called in Basque terms such as "paso", "embido" and "tira", and points are often kept with beans.

summary.en: Organised from Hangest-en-Santerre (Somme), hand ball is a direct descendant of the medieval jeu de paume: two teams hit the ball bare-handed across a long court with no net, where coloured stakes called chasses mark the line between the camps.

summary.en: In Tours-en-Vimeu (Somme), balle au tamis is a team game descended from jeu de paume: when serving, a player may bounce the very hard ball off a wire-mesh sieve on a tripod, and each side then tries to gain ground on the other.

summary.en: In Godewaersvelde (Nord), near the Belgian border, Flemish bowls is played on a concave lane, the bourloire, where a ball is rolled towards a copper disc set in the ground; once made of beaten earth mixed with dung, the lane is now concrete.

summary.en: Around Tourcoing and Wattrelos (Nord), bourle is a precision game akin to boule de fort: players roll a steel-rimmed wooden disc along a concave track, the bourloire, trying to stop it as close as possible to a small copper target.

summary.en: Played north of Amiens (Somme), ballon au poing is a ball game in which the ball is struck with the fist; like longue paume and hand ball, it belongs to the family of games descended from the old jeu de paume.

elements.title_fr: Le billon de Douai

location_sources.publisher: PCI Lab (ministère de la Culture, CIRDOC)

summary.en: In Douai (Nord), billon is a game of skill in which players throw a heavy hornbeam club weighing about three kilos towards a wooden post nine metres away, on a lane of damp sand edged with planks; the club closest to the post scores.

summary.en: In Boves (Somme), the game of guise, once a children's street game, involves striking a small pointed ash stick with a bat to flip it into the air and then drive it as far as possible; it is now often played on a straight road.

summary.en: The game of the assiette is a traditional Picard game played in Albert (Somme), where a players' association keeps it alive within the network of Picardy's traditional games.

summary.en: Played mainly in the Santerre (Somme), with a few clubs in the Oise and Paris, longue paume is a racket-and-ball sport on large outdoor grounds, often lined with lime trees, where stakes called chasses mark the ground won.

elements.title_fr: Le jeu de la bézette en Normandie

location_sources.publisher: Ministère de la Culture, fiche d'inventaire

image.credit: Moutte84
image.alt: Le jeu de la bézette en Normandie

summary.fr: La bézette est un jeu de dés de comptoir joué surtout dans l'Eure, en Normandie : chaque joueur tente de se défaire de ses 12 à 15 anneaux en les plaçant sur un petit mât de bois selon les dés obtenus ; des concours existent encore.
summary.en: Bézette is a counter dice game played mainly in the Eure, Normandy: each player tries to get rid of 12 to 15 rings by placing them on a small wooden post according to the dice thrown; competitions are still held.

summary_source.publisher: Fiche d'inventaire (ministère de la Culture)

elements.title_fr: Le jeu de la boule de hasard

location_sources.publisher: Ministère de la Culture, fiche d'inventaire

image.alt: Le jeu de la boule de hasard

summary.fr: Dans le Cotentin (Manche), ce jeu de comptoir et d'auberge consiste à lancer une boule sur un plateau de bois incliné, à travers un petit labyrinthe, jusqu'à l'une des quatre cases valant de 1 à 4 points ; une variante se jouait avec de l'argent.
summary.en: In the Cotentin (Manche), this bar and inn game sends a ball down a sloping wooden board, through a small maze, into one of four slots worth one to four points; one variant was played for money.

summary_source.publisher: PCI Lab (ministère de la Culture, CIRDOC)

elements.title_fr: Le jeu de la carambole à gouttière

location_sources.publisher: Ministère de la Culture, fiche d'inventaire

image.alt: Le jeu de la carambole à gouttière

summary.fr: Jeu de comptoir et d'argent du Bocage virois et de la région de Villedieu-les-Poêles (Manche), la carambole à gouttière consiste à lancer une petite boule par une gouttière sur une planche à rebords pour renverser six quilles et une quille centrale.
summary.en: A counter and gambling game from the Bocage around Vire and the Villedieu-les-Poêles area (Manche), carambole à gouttière sends a small ball down a chute onto a rimmed board to knock over six pins and a central one.

elements.title_fr: Le jeu de la crosse

location_sources.publisher: Ministère de la Culture, fiche d'inventaire

image.credit: Fiche d'inventaire du PCI (ministère de la Culture), via PCI Lab
image.alt: Le jeu de la crosse

summary.fr: Jeu normand pratiqué du Moyen Âge jusque vers 1942, souvent autour de Mardi gras, puis relancé en 2001, la crosse oppose des équipes qui poussent une balle, la « choule », avec une crosse ou au pied pour la faire passer dans un but appelé « viquet ».
summary.en: A Norman game played from the Middle Ages until around 1942, often at Shrovetide, and revived in 2001, crosse pits teams against each other as they drive a ball, the choule, with a stick or foot through a goal called the viquet.

summary_source.publisher: PCI Lab (ministère de la Culture, CIRDOC)

elements.title_fr: Le jeu de la grande carambole et du bastringue

location_sources.publisher: Ministère de la Culture, fiche d'inventaire

image.credit: Fiche d'inventaire du PCI (ministère de la Culture)
image.alt: Le jeu de la grande carambole et du bastringue

summary.fr: Dans le centre de la Normandie (pays d'Auge, pays d'Ouche, Perche, plaine de Caen), la grande carambole et le bastringue sont des jeux de quilles sur piste, à cinq ou trois quilles, longtemps joués pour de l'argent lors des fêtes de village et des comices.
summary.en: In central Normandy (Pays d'Auge, Pays d'Ouche, Perche, Caen plain), the grande carambole and the bastringue are skittle games played on a track with five or three pins, long played for money at village fairs and agricultural shows.

summary_source.publisher: Fiche d'inventaire (ministère de la Culture)

elements.title_fr: Le jeu de la grande choule

location_sources.publisher: Ministère de la Culture, fiche d'inventaire

image.credit: Fiche d'inventaire du PCI (ministère de la Culture), via PCI Lab
image.alt: Le jeu de la grande choule

summary.fr: En Normandie, la grande choule est un jeu collectif de balle au pied et à la main, attesté du Moyen Âge à 1914 et repris en 2004 : il se joue entre deux équipes qui cherchent à « noyer » la balle dans une mare.
summary.en: In Normandy, la grande choule is a team ball game played with feet and hands, recorded from the Middle Ages to 1914 and revived in 2004: two sides compete to "drown" the ball in a pond.

summary_source.publisher: PCI Lab (ministère de la Culture, CIRDOC)

location_sources.publisher: PCI Lab (ministère de la Culture, CIRDOC)

image.alt: Le jeu de la tèque

summary.fr: Dans l'est du Cotentin (Manche), la tèque est un jeu de balle et de bâton jadis joué l'après-midi de Mardi gras : un batteur frappe la balle lancée puis court autour de piquets avant que l'équipe adverse la renvoie à son capitaine.
summary.en: In the eastern Cotentin (Manche), tèque is a bat-and-ball game once played on Shrove Tuesday afternoon: a batter hits the thrown ball and then runs round a circuit of stakes before the fielding side can return it to their captain.

summary_source.publisher: PCI Lab (ministère de la Culture, CIRDOC)

elements.title_fr: Le jeu des treis soeus du Cotentin

location_sources.publisher: PCI Lab (ministère de la Culture, CIRDOC)

image.alt: Le jeu des treis soeus du Cotentin

summary.fr: Dans l'est du Cotentin, autour de Montebourg (Manche), le jeu des treis soeus consiste à renverser trois quilles coniques alignées en une ou deux boules lancées sans rouler au sol ; attesté depuis le XIXe siècle, il donne lieu à des concours locaux réguliers.
summary.en: In the eastern Cotentin, around Montebourg (Manche), the treis soeus game involves knocking down three cone-shaped skittles in a row with one or two balls thrown without rolling; recorded since the 19th century, it still has regular local contests.

image.alt: Le jeu du camembert

summary.fr: Venu du pays de Bray et de la région de Cherbourg et désormais joué dans toute la Normandie, le jeu du camembert consiste à faire glisser sur une longue planche des palets de bois verni de la taille d'un fromage, pour les arrêter sur les cases les mieux notées.
summary.en: Originating in the Pays de Bray and around Cherbourg and now played across Normandy, the camembert game involves sliding varnished wooden discs the size of the cheese along a long board so they stop on the highest-scoring squares.

location_sources.publisher: Ministère de la Culture, fiche d'inventaire

image.alt: Le jeu de ninepin bowling classic

summary.fr: Apparu à la fin du XIXe siècle, le ninepin bowling classic est un jeu de neuf quilles surtout pratiqué en Alsace et en Côte-d'Or : en 30 lancers, le joueur alterne « jeu plein », où les quilles sont relevées à chaque coup, et « déblayage ».
summary.en: Dating from the late 19th century, ninepin bowling classic is a nine-pin game played mainly in Alsace and the Côte-d'Or: over 30 throws, players alternate between full play, with all pins reset after each throw, and clearing play.

image.alt: Le jeu de ninepin bowling schere

summary.fr: Pratiqué en France surtout en Lorraine, ainsi que dans le Nord, les Vosges et les Ardennes, le ninepin bowling schere est un jeu de neuf quilles disposées en losange, chacune portant un nom selon sa place : quille de devant, dames, valets et roi au centre.
summary.en: Played in France mainly in Lorraine and also in the Nord, the Vosges and the Ardennes, ninepin bowling schere uses nine pins set in a diamond, each named after its position: front pin, queens, jacks and, in the middle, the king.

summary.fr: Héritière des jeux de longue paume, la balle au tambourin se pratique surtout dans l'Hérault et aussi à Gruissan et Narbonne (Aude) : deux équipes de cinq se renvoient une balle frappée avec un tambourin, souvent en plein air d'avril à septembre.
summary.en: Descended from longue paume, balle au tambourin is played mainly in the Hérault and also in Gruissan and Narbonne (Aude): two teams of five strike the ball back and forth with a tambourine-like bat, usually outdoors from April to September.

elements.title_fr: Le jeu de la boule lyonnaise

location_sources.publisher: Ministère de la Culture, fiche d'inventaire

image.alt: Le jeu de la boule lyonnaise

summary.fr: Joué dans toute la France et documenté ici à La Mure (Isère), le sport-boules ou boule lyonnaise consiste à placer ses boules au plus près d'un petit but, en pointant ou en tirant après une course d'élan ; il compte une forme traditionnelle et une forme sportive.
summary.en: Played throughout France and recorded here in La Mure (Isère), sport-boules or boule lyonnaise means landing one's bowls as close as possible to a small jack, either by pointing or by shooting after a run-up; it has traditional and athletic forms.

summary.en: In La Chapelle-d'Angillon (Cher), bordé is a woodcutters' game played in fine weather by teams of two, recalling the pairs who worked the big two-man saw: players throw a pointed hornbeam stick as close as possible to a stake 11 metres away.

summary.en: Every year on the first Sunday of August, the villages of the Montagne Bourbonnaise (Allier) compete in a friendly way at the Grands Jeux: tug of war, a woodcutters' contest and skittles, plus two games devised by the host village, often drawing on its history.

summary.en: In the Drôme, where one club based in Eurre remains, marble games draw on a worldwide children's pastime: in the classic version, two players roll their marbles towards a small hole in the ground and then flick them in.

summary.en: In Lavaur (Dordogne), a spring and a stone mark the old boundary of Périgord, Agenais and Quercy; legend says three bishops prayed there each in his own diocese, and since 2006 the bishops of Périgueux, Agen and Cahors have met there on Easter Monday.

summary.en: Among the Wayana and Apalai of French Guiana, the maraké is an initiation and alliance rite first undergone at puberty: a months-long cycle of ceremonies with kalawu songs, costumed dances and an ordeal of ant or wasp stings.

summary.en: On Cap Sizun (Finistère), a large granite block lying on the heath is said to be the stone boat on which Saint Conogan crossed the sea from Ireland; the legend passes by word of mouth and through storytelling walks.

summary.fr: Entre Plovan et Pouldreuzic, en pays Bigouden, un ensemble de pierres sur une colline est vu comme le « ménage » de saint Kodelig : son lit creusé dans la roche, son armoire et sa motte de beurre ; les promeneurs s'allongent encore dans l'empreinte du lit.
summary.en: Between Plovan and Pouldreuzic in the Bigouden country, a group of stones on a hill is seen as Saint Kodelig's household: his bed hollowed in the rock, his wardrobe and his pat of butter; walkers still lie down in the hollow of the bed.

summary.en: In Locronan (Finistère), a huge granite boulder known as the stone mare or Saint Ronan's chair is believed to help women who sit on it to conceive; it is one of the stops on the great troménie procession held every six years.

summary.en: Near the Saint-Vio chapel in Tréguennec, Bigouden country, an Iron Age stele is called Saint Vio's boat; until the interwar years, people turned one of its pieces over at Rogationtide to bring rain or fine weather.

summary.en: In Bieuzy-les-Eaux (Morbihan), in Saint Gildas's cave chapel above the Blavet, visitors strike a bell-like ringing stone with a pebble, circling it while making a wish; it was once said to heal the sick.

summary.en: On the banks of the Arguenon estuary at Le Guildo (Côtes-d'Armor), walkers strike rocks with pebbles to make them ring with a metallic sound; linked in legend to Gargantua, the stones have drawn visitors since the early 20th century.

summary.en: In the forest of Huelgoat (Finistère), visitors make a 137-tonne granite block, balanced on its edge, rock by pushing at one precise spot; the gesture and the stories around it make the site a stop on Breton tourist routes.

summary.en: In Trégunc (Finistère), three precariously balanced granite blocks rock under light pressure; each has its own virtue, like the Cuckolds' Stone or the Stone of Wealth, and making them move has been recorded for at least two centuries.

summary.en: In Allouville-Bellefosse, in the Pays de Caux, a very old oak a few metres from the church holds a chapel set up in its hollow trunk in the late 17th century; restored several times, the tree is at the heart of village life.

elements.title_fr: Le pèlerinage du Bas-Caumont

summary.en: In Bas-Caumont (Eure), on a slope above the Seine, a small chapel wraps around the base of a roughly 300-year-old oak; a Marian pilgrimage, abandoned in 1972, was revived there in 2008 and takes place at the end of May.

summary.en: In Bayeux (Calvados), trees and public gardens, from the botanical garden to the Liberty plane tree near the cathedral, carry strong symbolic weight, embodying the town's memory and its attachment to freedom and democracy.

summary.en: In Bouquetot, on the Roumois plateau (Eure), a white hawthorn about six centuries old stands at the heart of the village; though not itself an object of worship, it is a symbolic landmark for the commune's identity and its main festivities.

elements.title_fr: La forêt de Brotonne

summary.fr: La glyptique, art millénaire de graver et sculpter les pierres dures et fines (sceaux, camées, intailles), est pratiquée dans un atelier parisien ; la pierre est façonnée par abrasion au touret, et aucune formation spécifique n'existe plus en France depuis 1995.
summary.en: Glyptics, the age-old art of engraving and carving hard and semi-precious stones (seals, cameos, intaglios), is practised in a Paris workshop; the stone is shaped by abrasion on a lathe, and France has had no dedicated training since 1995.

summary_source.publisher: PCI Lab (ministère de la Culture, CIRDOC)

elements.title_fr: La gravure héraldique

location_sources.publisher: PCI Lab (ministère de la Culture, CIRDOC)

summary.fr: À Dinan (Côtes-d'Armor), un graveur héraldiste grave en creux des blasons sur des chevalières et des cachets en or ou en bronze, au burin et aux ciselets miniatures, en traduisant les couleurs en hachures et pointillés selon un code précis.
summary.en: In Dinan (Côtes-d'Armor), a heraldic engraver cuts coats of arms in intaglio into gold or bronze signet rings and seals with gravers and miniature chisels, rendering colours as hatching and dots according to a strict code.

summary_source.publisher: PCI Lab (ministère de la Culture, CIRDOC)

elements.title_fr: Le savoir-faire de la dentelle au point d'Alençon

location_sources.publisher: PCI Lab (ministère de la Culture, CIRDOC)

image.credit: René Dinkel
image.alt: Le savoir-faire de la dentelle au point d'Alençon

summary.fr: Le point d'Alençon (Orne) est une dentelle à l'aiguille faite entièrement à la main avec un seul fil, en assemblant invisiblement de petits éléments au fil de dix étapes ; une dizaine de spécialistes seulement le maîtrisent, pour la plupart à l'atelier conservatoire national d'Alençon.
summary.en: Point d'Alençon (Orne) is a needle lace made entirely by hand with a single thread, small elements being invisibly joined over ten stages; only about ten specialists master it, most of them at the national conservatory workshop in Alençon.

summary_source.publisher: PCI Lab (ministère de la Culture, CIRDOC)

elements.title_fr: La mégisserie à Saint-Junien (Haute-Vienne)

location_sources.publisher: PCI Lab (ministère de la Culture, CIRDOC)

image.credit: Lucas Destrem
image.alt: La mégisserie à Saint-Junien (Haute-Vienne)

summary.fr: À Saint-Junien (Haute-Vienne), ville de tradition gantière, une mégisserie installée au bord de la Vienne transforme des peaux de chevreau et d'agneau en cuir souple, par une longue suite d'opérations de délainage, de bains et de tannage.
summary.en: In Saint-Junien (Haute-Vienne), a town with a long glove-making tradition, a tawery on the banks of the Vienne turns kid and lamb skins into soft leather through a long series of dewooling, soaking and tanning steps.

summary_source.publisher: PCI Lab (ministère de la Culture, CIRDOC)

elements.title_fr: La peinture sur porcelaine à Saint-Junien (Haute-Vienne)

location_sources.publisher: PCI Lab (ministère de la Culture, CIRDOC)

image.credit: Fiche d'inventaire du PCI (ministère de la Culture), via PCI Lab
image.alt: La peinture sur porcelaine à Saint-Junien (Haute-Vienne)

summary.fr: À Saint-Junien (Haute-Vienne), un décorateur peint à la main de la porcelaine blanche achetée aux fabricants du Limousin : motif tracé au gabarit ou au poncif, couleurs préparées à partir de pigments, puis cuisson qui fixe le décor.
summary.en: In Saint-Junien (Haute-Vienne), a decorator hand-paints white porcelain bought from Limousin manufacturers: the motif is traced with a template or pounce, colours are mixed from pigments, and firing fixes the decoration.

summary_source.publisher: PCI Lab (ministère de la Culture, CIRDOC)

elements.title_fr: Le remplissage des maisons en pan de bois en Normandie

location_sources.publisher: PCI Lab (ministère de la Culture, CIRDOC)

image.credit: Fiche d'inventaire du PCI (ministère de la Culture), via PCI Lab
image.alt: Le remplissage des maisons en pan de bois en Normandie

summary.fr: En Normandie, un maçon remplit et décore les murs à pans de bois, surtout sur des monuments historiques, avec du torchis d'argile et de paille, un enduit « tapisserie » ou du tuileau, éclats de vieilles tuiles posés à la chaux en motifs géométriques.
summary.en: In Normandy, a mason fills and decorates timber-framed walls, mostly on listed buildings, with clay-and-straw daub, "tapestry" render or tuileau, fragments of old roof tiles set in lime in geometric patterns.

summary_source.publisher: PCI Lab (ministère de la Culture, CIRDOC)

elements.title_fr: L'héliogravure

location_sources.publisher: PCI Lab (ministère de la Culture, CIRDOC)

image.credit: Fiche d'inventaire du PCI (ministère de la Culture), via PCI Lab
image.alt: L'héliogravure

summary.fr: L'héliogravure transfère une image sur une plaque de cuivre grâce à une gélatine sensible à la lumière, avant gravure à l'acide et impression ; née au XIXe siècle pour la reproduction en nombre, elle est pratiquée dans un atelier de Meudon pour l'estampe d'art.
summary.en: Photogravure transfers an image onto a copper plate through light-sensitive gelatine before acid etching and printing; born in the 19th century for mass reproduction, it is practised in a workshop in Meudon for fine-art prints.

summary_source.publisher: PCI Lab (ministère de la Culture, CIRDOC)

elements.title_fr: Le repas gastronomique des Français

location_sources.publisher: Ministère de la Culture, communiqué du 19 juin 2013

image.credit: Fiche d'inventaire du PCI (ministère de la Culture), via PCI Lab
image.alt: Le repas gastronomique des Français

summary.fr: Partout en France, le repas gastronomique marque les grands moments de la vie, naissances, mariages ou retrouvailles ; il se distingue du quotidien par un menu choisi à l'avance, une table dressée avec soin et une suite de plats accordés aux vins.
summary.en: Across France, the gastronomic meal marks life's important moments such as births, weddings or reunions; it differs from everyday meals through a menu planned ahead, a carefully laid table and a sequence of courses matched with wines.

summary_source.publisher: PCI Lab (ministère de la Culture, CIRDOC)

elements.title_fr: La sculpture sur bois à Sainte-Soulle (Charente-Maritime)

location_sources.publisher: PCI Lab (ministère de la Culture, CIRDOC)

image.credit: Fiche d'inventaire du PCI (ministère de la Culture), via PCI Lab
image.alt: La sculpture sur bois à Sainte-Soulle (Charente-Maritime)

summary.fr: À Sainte-Soulle, près de La Rochelle (Charente-Maritime), un sculpteur ornemaniste reporte son dessin sur le bois, dégrossit la pièce puis la sculpte à la gouge avant ponçage, teinte et cire ; il réalise boiseries, bas-reliefs et statues, en création comme en restauration.
summary.en: In Sainte-Soulle, near La Rochelle (Charente-Maritime), an ornamental woodcarver transfers his drawing onto the wood, roughs out the piece and carves it with gouges before sanding, staining and waxing; he makes panelling, reliefs and statues, both new and restored.

summary_source.publisher: PCI Lab (ministère de la Culture, CIRDOC)

elements.title_fr: La tapisserie d'Aubusson (Creuse)

location_sources.publisher: PCI Lab (ministère de la Culture, CIRDOC)

image.credit: LucasD
image.alt: La tapisserie d'Aubusson (Creuse)

summary.fr: À Aubusson (Creuse), centre de tapisserie depuis près de six siècles avec Felletin, des lissiers tissent sur métier horizontal, de basse lisse, en suivant un carton grandeur nature dont chaque numéro renvoie à une couleur de laine ; une manufacture en propose près d'un millier.
summary.en: In Aubusson (Creuse), a tapestry centre for nearly six centuries along with Felletin, weavers work on horizontal low-warp looms, following a full-size cartoon in which each number stands for a wool colour; one manufactory stocks almost a thousand shades.

summary_source.publisher: PCI Lab (ministère de la Culture, CIRDOC)

elements.title_fr: Le tissage à bras

location_sources.publisher: PCI Lab (ministère de la Culture, CIRDOC)

image.credit: Bapppi
image.alt: Le tissage à bras

summary.fr: À Peillac (Morbihan), un atelier de tissage à bras produit sur des métiers actionnés à la main des pièces uniques, des tissus bretons traditionnels et des reconstitutions d'étoffes anciennes pour les musées ; aucune formation officielle n'existe en France pour ce métier.
summary.en: In Peillac (Morbihan), a hand-weaving workshop uses manually operated looms to make one-off pieces, traditional Breton fabrics and reconstructions of old textiles for museums; France has no official training for this trade.

summary_source.publisher: PCI Lab (ministère de la Culture, CIRDOC)

elements.title_fr: Le trait de charpente

location_sources.publisher: PCI Lab (ministère de la Culture, CIRDOC)

image.credit: Fiche d'inventaire du PCI (ministère de la Culture), via PCI Lab
image.alt: Le trait de charpente

summary.fr: Le trait de charpente rassemble les épures tracées à l'échelle ou grandeur nature, qui permettent de préparer au sol toutes les pièces d'une charpente avant le levage ; la fiche le décrit en Champagne-Ardenne, où il garde aussi un rôle symbolique chez les compagnons.
summary.en: Carpentry layout drawing ("trait de charpente") uses scale or full-size working drawings to prepare every timber of a roof frame on the ground before raising it; documented in Champagne-Ardenne, it also carries symbolic weight in the compagnonnage.

summary_source.publisher: PCI Lab (ministère de la Culture, CIRDOC)

elements.title_fr: Les savoir-faire du tourneur sur bois

location_sources.publisher: PCI Lab (ministère de la Culture, CIRDOC)

image.credit: Fiche d'inventaire du PCI (ministère de la Culture), via PCI Lab
image.alt: Les savoir-faire du tourneur sur bois

summary.fr: À Dinard (Ille-et-Vilaine), un tourneur sur bois façonne au tour des objets décoratifs dans des bois de pays, des bois exotiques ou des loupes ; les finitions (ponçage, lustrage, teintes naturelles, cire ou huile) occupent l'essentiel du temps de travail.
summary.en: In Dinard (Ille-et-Vilaine), a woodturner shapes decorative pieces on the lathe from local or exotic timbers and burls; finishing (sanding, buffing, natural stains, wax or oil) takes up most of the working time.

summary_source.publisher: PCI Lab (ministère de la Culture, CIRDOC)

elements.title_fr: Le compagnonnage

location_sources.publisher: Ministère de la Culture, fiche d'inventaire

image.credit: AlSepPhoenix
image.alt: Le compagnonnage

summary.fr: Le compagnonnage forme des hommes de métier tout en les faisant entrer dans une communauté aux rites et symboles propres, comme la canne ou les rubans ; le Tour de France, voyage de plusieurs années de ville en ville, en marque les étapes.
summary.en: The compagnonnage trains craftspeople while bringing them into a community with its own rites and symbols, such as the cane and ribbons; the Tour de France, several years of travel from town to town, marks each stage of their progress.

summary_source.publisher: PCI Lab (ministère de la Culture, CIRDOC)

elements.title_fr: L'émaillerie de Limoges (Haute-Vienne)

location_sources.publisher: PCI Lab (ministère de la Culture, CIRDOC)

image.credit: G.Garitan
image.alt: L'émaillerie de Limoges (Haute-Vienne)

summary.fr: À Limoges, où l'émail se serait développé dès le haut Moyen Âge, un émailleur pose des poudres d'émail sur une base de cuivre, parfois d'or ou d'argent, puis les cuit entre 850 et 900 °C ; certaines pièces passent jusqu'à dix fois au four.
summary.en: In Limoges, where enamelling probably took root in the early Middle Ages, an enameller lays powdered enamel on a copper base, sometimes gold or silver, and fires it at 850 to 900 °C; some pieces go into the kiln up to ten times.

summary_source.publisher: PCI Lab (ministère de la Culture, CIRDOC)

elements.title_fr: La céramique d'art à Château (Saône-et-Loire)

location_sources.publisher: Ministère de la Culture, fiche d'inventaire

image.alt: La céramique d'art à Château (Saône-et-Loire)

summary.fr: À Château, en Saône-et-Loire, un céramiste d'art prépare lui-même ses pâtes et broie ses émaux à partir de roches, cendres et argiles récoltées en carrière, puis tourne et cuit une porcelaine à 1300–1400 °C dans des fours qu'il conçoit.
summary.en: At Château in Saône-et-Loire, an art ceramist prepares his own clay bodies and grinds glazes from rocks, ashes and clays gathered in quarries, then throws and fires porcelain at 1300–1400 °C in kilns of his own design.

summary_source.publisher: Fiche d'inventaire (ministère de la Culture)

summary.en: In Chapaize (Saône-et-Loire), a gilding workshop restores mirrors, frames and carvings for museums; the craft combines joinery, carving, modelling and laying gold leaf over a dozen coats of chalk and hide-glue ground.

summary.en: In Came (Pyrénées-Atlantiques), a workshop makes and restores traditional and period chairs to order, drawing on local craftspeople: carvers, turners, rush-seaters and caners.

summary.en: In Saint-André-le-Désert, Burgundy, studio ceramists make one-off stoneware and porcelain pieces; one prepares his own clays and grinds glazes from rocks, ashes and clays, judging the firing by the colour of the flame.

summary.en: In Saône-et-Loire, a workshop builds and restores 18th- and 19th-century fortepianos and clavichords using period materials and methods; a single copy takes thousands of hours, after the wood has seasoned for several years.

summary.en: In Paris, bespoke tailoring relies on some fifteen measurements, cutting, several fittings and mostly hand stitching; in larger workshops the cutter, coat-maker, trouser-maker, waistcoat-maker and buttonhole-maker share the work.

summary.en: In Bourdettes (Pyrénées-Atlantiques), a family workshop hammers sheet metal into bells for livestock and hunting dogs, brazes them with brass inside clay moulds, then tunes them by ear.

summary.en: In Donzy-le-Pertuis (Saône-et-Loire), a craftsman selects trees in the forest for instrument making, seasons their wood for around fifteen years and supplies it to makers; he also builds and restores instruments, especially the hurdy-gurdy.

summary.en: In Lower Normandy, potters shape glazed earthenware finials in plaster moulds, ornaments that have crowned house roofs since the Middle Ages; the skill is now hard to pass on.

summary_source.publisher: PCI Lab (ministère de la Culture, CIRDOC)

elements.title_fr: La porcelaine de Limoges (Haute-Vienne)

summary.en: In Limoges (Haute-Vienne), porcelain starts from a plaster model enlarged to allow for shrinkage; pieces are slip-cast, glazed and fired at around 1400 °C. The kaolin it relies on was found at Saint-Yrieix-la-Perche in 1768.

summary.en: In the Basque Country, the xare is a pelota racket made from a bent hazel stem forming the frame and a pocket of knotted string resembling a spider's web; the maker adjusts its curve to the player's position and to whether they are right- or left-handed.

summary.en: In Pyrénées-Atlantiques, notably in Morlanne, the pelèra brings relatives and friends together over three days to slaughter the family pig and turn it into cured meat, black pudding, pâtés and sausages; helpers are then treated to a meal.

summary.en: In Larrau (Pyrénées-Atlantiques), livestock farmers in isolated mountain houses have kept a lore of plants, animals and sometimes ritual healing gestures to treat people and animals; it is fading but still remembered.

summary.en: In Fougerolles (Haute-Saône), at the foot of the Vosges, kirsch, a cherry brandy, has been distilled since the late 18th century. The fruit comes from tall-tree meadow orchards that combine grazing and fruit growing, and a whole community has grown up around distilling.

summary.en: The cooking of the Nice area (Alpes-Maritimes) counts over two hundred recipes from both sea and mountain, using chard, round courgettes or basil. It blends Ligurian, Piedmontese and Provençal influences, as in the local stockfish dishes.

summary.en: In Upper Brittany, the craquelin is a dry scalded biscuit shaped like a small crunchy bowl; five makers still produce it in about a dozen steps, from scalding to baking, and it is eaten sweet or savoury.

summary.fr: Dans les marais salants de la presqu'île de Guérande et du sud du Morbihan, les paludiers récoltent le sel selon des gestes peu changés depuis des siècles, au cœur d'un paysage façonné par l'homme où se mêlent pêche, cueillette et fêtes.
summary.en: In the salt marshes of the Guérande peninsula and southern Morbihan, salt workers harvest salt with methods little changed over centuries, in a man-made landscape that also supports fishing, gathering and festivities.

image.alt: Les savoir-faire de la découpe bouchère à la française

summary.fr: Née à Paris au XIXe siècle et devenue la référence nationale, la découpe bouchère à la française repose sur une connaissance fine de l'anatomie pour tirer de chaque muscle des morceaux adaptés à la cuisine ; elle se transmet par l'apprentissage.
summary.en: Developed in Paris in the 19th century and now the national standard, French-style butchery cutting relies on detailed knowledge of anatomy to turn each muscle into cuts suited to different dishes; it is passed on through apprenticeship.

summary.en: In the Baronnies provençales, lime-blossom picking, which began in the late 19th century for herbal medicine and perfumery, involves grafting, pruning, picking and drying skills that bring several generations together each summer.

summary.fr: À Chirongui, à Mayotte, quelques femmes extraient le Tani Malandi, une argile blanche kaolinique, et la façonnent en pains ; elle sert au maquillage festif des mariées, aux soins traditionnels et aux rituels où les guérisseurs communiquent avec les esprits.

image.alt: Pratiques de pêche passives sur le bassin Loire

summary.fr: Sur la Loire, de la Nièvre à la Loire-Atlantique, une dizaine de pêcheurs professionnels utilisent encore le guideau, filet tendu la nuit depuis un bateau fixe pour l'anguille lors des crues, et le filet-barrage, posé au printemps pour l'alose.
summary.en: On the Loire, from the Nièvre to Loire-Atlantique, about ten professional fishers still use the guideau, a net set at night from a moored boat to catch eels during floods, and the barrier net, laid in spring for shad.

image.credit: New York Fashion TV
image.alt: La haute couture

summary.fr: Née à Paris au milieu du XIXe siècle, la haute couture désigne la création de pièces uniques entièrement sur mesure dans des ateliers en France, où modélistes, toilistes et premières mains se partagent le travail ; les collections sont présentées deux fois par an à Paris.
summary.en: Born in Paris in the mid-19th century, haute couture is the making of one-off, fully made-to-measure garments in French workshops, where pattern makers, toile makers and head seamstresses share the work; collections are shown twice a year in Paris.

image.alt: Les jours ou broderie de Cilaos

summary.fr: Les jours de Cilaos, à La Réunion, sont une broderie blanche ajourée très fine née au début du XXe siècle : on retire des fils de la toile puis on brode des motifs inspirés de la faune et de la flore de l'île, surtout dans le Cirque de Cilaos.
summary.en: Cilaos openwork, on Réunion Island, is a very fine white embroidery that emerged in the early 20th century: threads are drawn from the cloth and the gaps re-embroidered with motifs taken from local plants and animals, mainly in the Cirque de Cilaos.

image.alt: Les savoir-faire de la construction en terre crue en France

summary.fr: Partout en France, hexagone et outre-mer, la construction en terre crue rassemble des savoir-faire allant du choix d'une terre locale à sa mise en œuvre en murs, cloisons ou sols, comme la bauge ou le torchis ; après un net déclin, elle connaît un regain depuis une quarantaine d'années.
summary.en: Across France, mainland and overseas, earth building gathers skills that run from choosing a local soil to using it for walls, partitions or floors, as in cob or wattle and daub; after a sharp decline, it has seen renewed interest for some forty years.

image.alt: La fabrication de cravaches et de fouets à Sorède (Pyrénées-Orientales)

summary.fr: À Sorède (Pyrénées-Orientales), on fabrique depuis le Moyen Âge des fouets et cravaches en bois de micocoulier tressé à la vapeur ; après la fermeture des dernières fabriques, le savoir-faire est maintenu par un établissement d'aide par le travail.
summary.en: At Sorède (Pyrénées-Orientales), whips and riding crops have been made from steam-braided hackberry wood since the Middle Ages; after the last factories closed, the craft has been kept alive by a sheltered-employment workshop.
